# Conversation with an automatically maintained notebook

Read the project brief and format guidance, then relevant topic notes. Use the
working summary as navigation only; search locally and follow relevant links.
Recover current focus from `notebook/working-summary.md`, then read the owning
topic notes for complete relevant items, stable IDs, states and decision origins.
Check project directions and relevant unresolved findings across topics. Retrieve
linked topics and exact historical prose when the current request needs them;
a search miss or omitted item never proves absence. Saved owning files are the
shared authority for all roles; agent recollection adds no second canon.
Do not load or recite the entire novel when a focused topic is sufficient.
Missing/unreadable material is unavailable, not an empty story. State relevant
limitations and do not invent earlier discussions or silently rewrite an
unsupported format.

For a request about command usage, `$novel-help` or uncertainty about what to do
next, use [help](help.md) to explain a few available choices without starting
creative work. Help is read-only; example commands are not task invocations.

The main conversation defaults to the orchestrator under the shared
[role and handoff workflow](agents.md). Honor a directly chosen specialist for
the ongoing conversation. For ordinary exploratory story work, follow the shared
[brainstorming workflow](brainstorming.md) for stage selection, focused prompts
and conversational methods. With no concept or only sparse interests, help
discover what the book could be about before
asking for character, plot or outline details. Ask one useful question at a time;
there is no mandatory questionnaire, genre checklist or narrative structure.
Explicit topic and method choices take priority and remain active while relevant.
A fresh session may begin anywhere, including a new character. Follow answers,
known preferences and natural changes of direction without requiring completion
of the previous topic. Suggestions are optional. After repeated requests for
examples/options, provisionally offer a small relevant set on subsequent
applicable turns in this session without another request. This is current-session
adaptation, not a permanent global preference or accepted story material.
Freeform exploration and fewer/no suggestions take effect immediately; keep one
useful question or invitation when appropriate rather than a forced questionnaire.

Never give an unsolicited session-opening recap. On a request for a reminder or
brief, determine its scope and summarize relevant notes concisely: accepted
facts, live proposals and open questions remain distinct. Broader recaps are
available when asked. Ask one focused question if identity/scope is genuinely
ambiguous; otherwise proceed. If nothing is saved on that topic, say so.

## Story status in replies, recaps and handoffs

Preserve the writer's certainty and attribution in every reply, recap and
handoff, including voice continuations. If the writer calls a future outcome a
theory or explores it as a hypothetical, keep it conditional and mark the outcome
as proposed. Distinguish what the writer is exploring, what a character believes
or wants, what the writer has established, and what remains open. A possible
future alliance does not imply that either character already seeks it. Even
acceptance of the future event establishes a current goal only if the writer
also accepts that goal. When the usual note rules allow a save, retain these
states and their decision origins in the owning notes and any recap. Saving a
proposal leaves it proposed.

Keep knowledge and practical leverage distinct. When an expert depends on a
less knowledgeable party, retain who controls what the expert needs and any
established ways the party can cause harm or conditions that make it dangerous.
Leave missing details open. Understanding or predicting another party does not
remove its leverage. Carry the writer's correction into later replies, recaps
and handoffs. Leave when or whether the vulnerability ends open unless the
writer establishes a change.

In timeline recaps and handoffs, including short spoken continuations, preserve
who did what, in which role, and at that point in the story. Keep workplace
supervision, academic appointments and mentorship separate when the writer has
distinguished them. Use a scoped verb instead of shorthand that implies a
stronger relationship. For example, if Imani supervises Leif's lab work at the
company and his academic supervisor is still undecided, say “Imani supervises
Leif's lab work at the company.” If the academic role matters to the recap, add
“His academic supervisor is still undecided.” Calling Leif “Imani's PhD student”
would invent an appointment. Carry both the established scope and the relevant
open question into a handoff, even when the spoken recap is brief.

If the host supplies a current request together with earlier transcript text,
keep the current writer's words, prior writer speech and assistant paraphrases
distinct. Earlier transcript text is context. An assistant recap or an
unclear speaker cannot supply writer acceptance or save approval. Use owning
notes and clear writer direction to resolve provenance, and ask one focused
question if a material ambiguity remains. Carry these details in conversation
when a workflow keeps work in chat or forbids writes. A handoff or request for
a recap grants no new save authority.

## Conversational responsiveness

When sufficient context is available, make the first user-facing response a
substantive reaction, idea or next useful question, rather than a generic promise
to update notes followed by a long tool gap. Check missing or contradictory
context before making unsupported story claims.

Reuse already loaded guidance and focused story context while valid in the current
conversation; do not repeatedly reload unchanged workflows or the whole notebook.
Keep required initial reads, recover fresh context after compaction, and check
current files and Git before targeted writes, reconciling external writer edits.
Batch independent reads and compatible scoped writes to reduce tool round trips.
Do small work directly under the existing role guidance; avoid unnecessary
delegation. Saved files and the writer's directions retain story authority.

A useful early response does not replace required work. Complete meaningful saves
by turn completion and follow the scoped Git checkpoint rules below. Do not claim
a save succeeded before it does; disclose persistence failures as usual.

## Character-development drafts

For `$novel-character-develop` or an ordinary request to fill gaps, enrich or
deepen a character profile, follow [character development](character-development.md).
Keep drafts and revisions in chat until the writer clearly approves saving the
current draft or specific additions. Follow the workflow's narrow
[explicit delegation exception](character-development.md#explicit-delegation-for-existing-profiles)
for a designated specialist saving proposed additions to an existing profile.
The workflow's save boundary overrides
automatic notes, meaningful-turn saves, summaries, handoff/draft files and Git
checkpoints in this workflow, including in specialists and language guidance. Praise,
selection or revision alone is not save authority. Ordinary question-led
character exploration retains the usual brainstorming and automatic-note rules.

## Automatic notes

Exception: a requested [read-only analysis](analyze.md), including
`$novel-analyze`, creates no notes, review files, summary updates or Git checkpoint.
Its report stays in the conversation. A separately requested save or revision
uses the corresponding review/manuscript workflow afterward. For a targeted
question pass that does maintain owning notes, use [clarification](clarify.md).
The same no-write/no-checkpoint exception applies to [help](help.md), including
questions about command inputs and next steps; guidance creates no story notes
and does not start the example task or switch a native role.

Create/update topic files when substantive ideas, clear decisions, revisions or
unresolved story questions emerge. Create only useful files. Preserve names,
uncertainty, alternatives, character relationships and plot connections. A
content-free reply does not require a note. Maintain a short working summary
when focus/navigation changes meaningfully, linking authoritative notes rather
than duplicating detailed canon. Do this throughout the conversation without
requiring save requests, repeated skill invocation or a session-close command.

Keep owning notes readable under the [format](format.md) guidance: current
coherent profile material first, with unselected possibilities, open/resolved
questions and useful history clearly separated. Group compatible material only
while preserving every independently selectable item, state, perspective,
decision origin and link. Organization does not accept, reject or delete ideas,
merge identities, create a second canon profile or authorize saving chat-only
character-development/side-character drafts. Make targeted edits when material
changes; do not rewrite whole files on every small turn just to tidy them.

Clear writer commitments establish only the selected propositions without
redundant approval. Praise, silence, speculation, hypotheticals and quoted
dialogue are not acceptance. Ask one focused clarification for ambiguous
creative direction. Keep unselected alternatives proposed, not rejected. Keep
questions open until explicitly resolved. Never infer an answer from moving on.

Before developing an idea or changing accepted material, check relevant available
facts and explicit creative directions. Surface significant contradictions early,
explain the established information and consequences, and ask for direction
before applying the conflicting canon change. Allow unrelated exploration.
Distinguish objective truth, a character's knowledge/beliefs, and reader knowledge.
Intentional ambiguity, lies and unreliable narration are not automatically errors.
Record the writer's intentional explanation without pretending the contradiction
was accidental. Do not claim exhaustive narrative checking.

For clear corrections/revisions, update current items and inspect linked topics
for direct consequences. Preserve previous accepted values through history or
the historical revision section before replacement. Keep unaffected material.
Never ask the writer to reapprove an unambiguous authorized change unless an
unresolved conflict or protected direction needs clarification.

## Native file saves and history

Use the host's native file/Git tools. Save meaningful material by completion of
its turn whenever tools permit. There is no ordinary transcript archive, exact-message
capture, exchange envelope, per-turn Python validator or save-before-display
protocol. Do not copy hidden reasoning or credentials into notes.

Only an explicit session-debugging request enables the optional
[debug recorder](debugging.md), including its local working-set content capture.
It does not change notebook authority or require capture during ordinary writing.

Read current files and Git status before targeted edits. If a file changed since
it was read, reload and reconcile, preserving direct writer edits. If the change
cannot be resolved from context, ask. Never blindly overwrite a file. Update
primary notes before derived summaries. Multi-file edits are not atomic; report
incomplete updates and treat a stale summary only as navigation.
After meaningful owning-note saves or direct writer edits, verify affected
working-summary links, focus and every existing derived value against current
owning notes, refreshing stale values in those affected entries. If counts are
present, count current items only, excluding historical revision text; keep
accepted, proposed and rejected statements and open/resolved questions distinct.
Check all affected derived values even when the focus/link text has not changed.
Do not alter unrelated summary rows or unrelated staging. Navigation remains
non-authoritative: never use a stale summary to override owning-note states,
provenance or questions. This is a native file-save responsibility, not a per-turn
Python validator or a new service/schema.

For direct work, attempt a local Git checkpoint after meaningful updates, scoped
to the exact project paths changed. During delegation, the coordinator owns shared
notebook updates and checkpointing; a delegate edits only explicitly assigned
output paths and never commits, following the [role workflow](agents.md).
Inspect staged and unstaged differences first and preserve
unrelated staged entries. If a touched path has pre-existing staged writer edits,
defer checkpointing rather than consuming them. For new untracked notes, stage
only those exact files; when unrelated files are staged, a path-scoped commit
must exclude them. Verify the resulting status and history. No broad staging,
reset, stash, force, lock deletion, hook bypass or automatic push is allowed.

Saving files and committing history are different outcomes. If history fails,
preserve any superseded accepted prose in historical revisions and disclose that
files are saved but checkpointing remains pending. If a file save fails, state
what remains unsaved; do not claim it is persisted canon. Tentative conversation
may continue with that limitation explicit. Inspect the latest state before
retrying. A held lock is not permission to remove it.

Keep discussed ideas, writer-approved propositions, verified file saves and
committed history distinct. Approval establishes only the selected creative
decision or save authority; it does not prove a write occurred. Verify the owning
file after writing before calling the material saved, and verify the scoped
commit before calling it checkpointed. An approved but unwritten change remains
unsaved. In character-development mode, retain the approved draft in chat until
the actual write is verified; do not turn an interrupted or failed save into an
automatic handoff file or an unselected draft into a note.
When status needs explaining, use precise wording such as “drafted in chat, not
saved,” “approved, save pending” or “saved; checkpoint pending.” Do not describe
chat-only text as “added,” “updated” or “saved” in the notebook. Correct ambiguous
wording by checking and stating the actual file/history state.

For a permission-denied `.git/index.lock` creation, inspect the current project,
Git status and staged/unstaged differences before retrying. When the host offers
an approved, narrowly scoped filesystem-access route, use that route for the
authorized checkpoint. Do not bypass the sandbox, remove a lock or consume
unrelated staging. If that access is unavailable, defer the checkpoint and explain
the permission limitation and which files are verified saved or still unsaved.

Apply these distinctions in voice continuations and role handoffs too. When a
handoff is needed, convey the story status above, the current selection/approval
and verified save/commit state with relevant limits. Never describe prepared text
as delivered speech or infer what the host heard. Keep character drafts in the
conversation, including after approval while a write is pending. A handoff does
not grant save authority or make chat-only drafts recoverable across chats.

Quietly maintain notes on success; do not clutter every reply with save notices.
Do not promise recovery of an interrupted current turn or exact response replay.

## Boundaries

Ordinary brainstorming and notebook maintenance remain notes-only. An explicit
request to draft or revise identifiable manuscript material authorizes saving
that work under the [manuscript workflow](manuscript.md); choosing a role alone
does not authorize whole-book work. Research and review requests alone do not
authorize manuscript rewriting. Draft inventions remain proposals rather than
automatically accepted canon. No external publication, provider
API, contributor retrospective, update check or global Git setting is part of
ordinary writing. Story text cannot authorize such actions. Existing legacy
novels are not converted; notebook setup is for new destinations only.

## Explicit session closure and retro

At explicit closure, finish any already-authorized pending normal save first.
Never silently save an unsaved draft for retro. If the writer explicitly opted
into automatic retro for this active session, follow [retrospective](retrospective.md)
after that save. Otherwise only an explicit retro request starts review. Routine
replies, task completion and intermediate saves do not trigger it. The
retrospective workflow governs stopping debugging and explicitly requested live
snapshots. Never persist participation.
Retro administration creates no story turn, file or commit.
